title: Project Overview
description: The README provides the essential context for understanding Servo: a prototype web browser engine written in Rust. It covers the project's goals, platform support (macOS, Linux, Windows, Android, OpenHarmony), and points to the Servo Book for detailed documentation. This is the starting point for anyone learning the codebase, as it explains why Servo exists and how its community operates.

title: Workspace Architecture
description: The root Cargo.toml defines the workspace structure that organizes Servo into 11 member crates, each responsible for a distinct subsystem: layout, script, net, canvas, media, SVG engine, and more. With over 250 workspace dependencies managed centrally, this file reveals how the project is decomposed into composable units and how external dependencies like Stylo (the CSS engine) are integrated through patches. Understanding this crate map is essential before exploring any single component.

title: Layout Engine Entry Point
description: The layout crate's lib.rs is the public API surface for the entire layout engine. It re-exports core types such as ConstraintSpace, ContainingBlock, and PropagatedBoxTreeData, which form the vocabulary used throughout the layout system. As the top-ranked code entry point by structural analysis, this file provides the bird's-eye view of how the layout crate exposes its functionality to the rest of the browser engine, including the constellation and script threads.
languageLesson: Rust lib.rs files serve dual roles: they declare the crate's module tree with 'pub mod' statements and re-export selected types with 'pub use' to define the public API. Items marked 'pub(crate)' are visible within the crate but not to external consumers, creating a layered visibility boundary.

title: Core Geometry and Layout Context
description: The geom module defines the logical geometry types (LogicalVec2, LogicalRect, LogicalSides) that underpin all spatial calculations in the layout engine, while the context module provides the per-layout execution environment including image resolution, caching, and parallel processing configuration. These two files establish the fundamental data structures everything else builds upon -- every box position, size, and margin in Servo traces back to these geometry primitives.

title: Box Tree Construction
description: The construct_modern module implements the algorithm that builds the layout box tree from DOM nodes, with support for parallel processing across threads. The LayoutBoxBase type provides the fundamental per-fragment box state, tracking inline content sizes, cache management for independent formatting contexts, and fragment storage. Together these files bridge the gap between the DOM's element tree and Servo's box-based layout representation, making them the first major step in the rendering pipeline.

title: CSS Flow Layout
description: The flow module is the heart of CSS layout in Servo, providing the box and fragment base types along with traversal state and formatting context plumbing. The formatting_contexts module defines the independent and block formatting context types that control how elements arrange themselves according to CSS rules. Understanding flow layout is essential because it handles the default rendering mode for web content -- block elements stacking vertically, inline elements flowing horizontally, and floats disrupting the normal flow.

title: Inline Text Layout
description: The inline formatting context module manages line-by-line layout of text and inline-level elements, coordinating fragment placement, text runs, and line breaking. The text_run module handles the low-level details of text shaping and glyph storage, converting Unicode text into positioned glyph runs. This is where text actually gets measured and placed onto lines, handling everything from kerning to bidirectional text reordering.

title: Fragment Tree and Display Lists
description: The fragment tree module barrel re-exports all fragment tree types that represent the output of layout -- a tree of positioned, sized fragments ready for painting. The display list module converts this fragment tree into WebRender display items, which are the platform-agnostic drawing commands that the GPU renderer executes. This step completes the layout-to-painting pipeline: boxes are constructed, flowed, measured, and finally converted into drawable primitives.

title: SVG Rendering Pipeline
description: The SVG engine is a separate rendering pipeline that handles SVG content, which has fundamentally different layout and rendering rules compared to HTML. The crate's entry point declares modules for style resolution, render tree construction, and shape extraction. The render_tree module defines the SvgRenderTree and SvgRenderNode data structures that represent the SVG document as a tree of renderable nodes with viewport information. This engine processes SVG shapes (paths, circles, rectangles, polygons) through tessellation and renders them via WebRender.

title: Script Engine and DOM Bindings
description: The script crate is one of Servo's largest components, implementing the DOM specification and providing JavaScript runtime bindings through WebIDL code generation. Its lib.rs re-exports all public submodules covering the full DOM API: elements, events, networking (fetch), storage, canvas, WebGL, WebGPU, WebXR, and more. This crate is where the browser's JavaScript engine integration lives, and it communicates with the layout and constellation threads through well-defined IPC channels.

title: Networking Stack
description: The net crate implements Servo's HTTP networking stack, handling resource loading, caching, cookie management, and protocol handlers. Its lib.rs re-exports submodules for HTTP loading, WebSockets, data URLs, file URLs, and the MIME classifier. Every web page, image, stylesheet, and script that Servo loads passes through this crate, making it the gateway between the browser engine and the internet.

title: Build Tooling and Toolchain
description: The rust-toolchain.toml pins Servo to Rust nightly 1.95.0 with required components including clippy, rustfmt, and the rust-src and rustc-dev components needed for build system tooling. The pyproject.toml configures the Python-based build tooling (Ruff linting, Pyrefly type-checking, setuptools for Python scripts). These configuration files reveal how Servo's build is orchestrated: Rust nightly for cutting-edge language features, Python scripts for development workflow tooling (mach commands, CI, testing), and strict toolchain versioning to ensure reproducible builds.
